what: HC up investigation with stop rule: establish the real bytes/efficiency, then test whether a grid/ILP shape reaches a gate-clearing ceiling

byte_calibration.engine_bytes: w_up is bf16 [10240][320] = 6.5536 MB per (layer, half) - the bench's 3.48 MB Q8_0 synthetic was the artifact
byte_calibration.in_situ: hc0 up 0.76 ms + hc1 up 0.74 ms per window at T=3.17; 96 calls => 15.6 us/call = ~415-420 GB/s = 56% of the 750 GB/s wall
byte_calibration.correction: the earlier 21-32% was the synthetic-Q8_0 bench; the engine's real efficiency is 56%

bench.tool: src/kernels/hc_up_bench.cpp (new diagnostics bench, not in the engine)
bench.run: one window, 300 iters, 6.55 MB bf16, 16 copies (105 MB, past LLC)
bench.best: V2 (row-split 4) = 11.6 us = 566 GB/s = 75% of the wall

bound.wall_ceiling: at 750 GB/s the 96 calls would take 0.83 ms instead of 1.50 => 0.67 ms saved = 1.9% of the 35 ms round - below the 2% gate even at the wall
bound.caveat: the bench's V0 replica (182 GB/s) is 2.3x slower than the engine's actual multi-token kernel (415), so the bench measures a shape effect, not the engine's exact headroom

verdict: STOPPED by the stop rule: even the theoretical wall (1.9%) cannot clear the pre-declared >=2% gate, and the practical best shape reaches 75% (1.2-1.4%). No engine change was made; the bench is kept as a diagnostic.
next: the campaign's remaining small-shape inefficiencies are all below the gate individually; a gate-clearing step needs a multi-call change (or a different objective)
